newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures finish mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures finish mostly lower.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished mostly lower in thin trade ahead of the U.S. consumer price index (CPI) on Tuesday, traders and analysts said.

Most of the floor action was confined to the Mexican peso pit, where options on futures were actively traded. Some floor sources said banks showed buying interest in March peso futures at $0.123872 and one large U.S. retail firm sold 500 contracts at the daily high of $0.124000.
Other currencies remained on the defensive, including sterling, which came under heavy dealer selling but remains long-term bullish.
Canadian dollars turned briefly lower but regained footing to the upside.
Most analysts said the uptrend for sterling and Canadian dollars was intact, with March sterling poised to test $1.70 in the near term and resistance at the contract high of $1.7128.
March Canadian dollars, meanwhile, are forecast to advance to $0.7504, which is roughly equivalent to 1.3382 spot, and possibly to $0.7550, or 1.33 spot, in the intermediate term.
"Canadian has really turned around," a trader said.
One local firm bought about 300 contracts late in the day.
Some traders said that March Canadian dollar's ability to hold above resistance at $0.7440, even during the contract's brief decline, was impressive and portended near-term gains.
"But I don't think it will be a quick rally," one currency futures floor source said, adding that once $0.7550 were violated, the contract could gain momentum to the upside and test $0.7600.
March marks and Swiss francs remained down, but traded off contract lows at $0.6305 and $0.7291, respectively.
Both currencies remained locked in a strong downtrend, as the dollar rose near a key trendline level against the mark at 1.5935 spot. The 1.5935 level represents a downtrend line from July 1989.

Traders said a stronger-than-expected increase in the U.S. consumer price index could weaken the dollar. They are looking for overall CPI to rise 0.3 percent and core CPI to increase 0.2 percent, the same as November's gains.
A CPI report that matches trade expectations could spark a fresh round of buying, they added.
Yen futures are also bearish in the long term, but the downward trend had less of a grip on the March contract than in other currencies.
Support for March yen is at $0.008649, which corresponds to 116.65 spot yen.

At the end of pit trade, March yen was down $0.000026 to $0.008670, marks were $0.0014 lower at $0.6324, Swiss francs were $0.0002 lower to $0.7319, pounds were off $0.0032 to $1.6718, Canadian dollars were $0.0006 higher at $0.7452, Aussie dollars fell $0.0029 to $0.7779 and pesos were off $0.000050 to $0.123525.
